title: Whole list is loaded once and overwritten on every save, so a second tab erases the first tab's recipes
evidence: recipes is read once at app.js:3. Every add and delete writes the entire in-memory array back with saveRecipes (app.js:24, 35). There is no 'storage' event listener and no re-read before the write.
failing_case: Open the page in tab A and tab B, both empty. Add "Soup" in A (storage holds [Soup]). Add "Pie" in B: B's array is [Pie] and it overwrites storage. Soup is gone for good. A reload shows only Pie.
remediation: Re-read the stored list immediately before each mutation and write the merged result, or listen for the 'storage' event and refresh recipes. Keep one writer per record.

title: parseInt on a type=number value turns exponent input into the wrong number
evidence: The input is type=number min=1 max=600 (index.html:17). Browsers accept "1e2" as a valid number and constraint validation passes. parseInt("1e2", 10) is 1, not 100. Number("1e2") is 100.
failing_case: The user types 1e2 in Minutes and submits. The recipe is saved with 1 minute, and the status reports a wrong total.
remediation: Use valueAsNumber (or Number) and check Number.isInteger(minutes) && minutes >= 1 && minutes <= 600. The JS check should enforce the same bounds as the HTML attributes.

title: Delete ignores a failed save and still announces "Deleted"
evidence: app.js:35 discards the boolean that saveRecipes (store.js:13-20) returns. app.js:36 then sets the status to Deleted unconditionally. The add handler at app.js:24-25 does check the result, so the two paths are inconsistent.
failing_case: Storage is full or blocked (private mode, quota). The user deletes a recipe. setItem throws, saveRecipes returns false, the UI removes the row and announces "Deleted ...". After a reload the recipe is back, because storage still holds the old list.
remediation: Check the return value of saveRecipes in the delete handler and show the same storage-failure message as the add path. Do not claim persistence that did not happen.

title: Deleting a recipe re-renders the list and drops keyboard focus to the page body
evidence: The delete handler (app.js:29-38) activates a button inside li, then render() replaces listEl.innerHTML, which destroys the focused button. Nothing moves focus afterwards. WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A) is affected.
failing_case: A keyboard user tabs to the third Delete and confirms. Focus resets to the document start. They must tab through the heading and form again to reach the next recipe. A screen reader loses its position, though it does hear the status text.
remediation: After rendering, focus the next row's Delete button, or the previous one, or the list heading when the list is empty. Alternatively remove just the deleted li.

quote: return Array.isArray(data) ? data.filter((r) => r && typeof r.name === "string") : [];
title: Load validates only name, so records missing id or minutes give NaN totals, "undefined" ids and a crash on Delete
evidence: store.js:7 keeps any object with a string name. totalMinutes (store.js:23) sums r.minutes, so a record without a numeric minutes gives NaN. render (app.js:10) writes data-id="undefined" via escapeHtml(undefined). The delete handler (app.js:32) then runs recipes.find(x => x.id === "undefined"), which finds nothing, and describe(r) at app.js:33 reads r.name from undefined. The comment at app.js:14 says describe's argument is never null, which this case contradicts.
failing_case: localStorage 'recipes' = [{"name":"Soup"}] (a shape from an older version or a hand edit). Page shows "Soup NaN min". Clicking Delete throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name'). The row can't be removed. Adding any recipe shows "Total cooking time: NaN minutes".
remediation: Normalise at the storage boundary: drop or repair each record so it has a string id (generate one), a finite positive minutes and a string name. Add a version field to the saved shape.

quote: return [];  // storage blocked or corrupt: start empty; app.js tells the user
title: Comment says app.js tells the user about corrupt or blocked storage, but nothing does; the next save then overwrites the corrupt data
evidence: loadRecipes returns [] for every failure (store.js:9). app.js:3 uses the result with no signal, and no other code mentions a load failure. The first successful saveRecipes replaces the stored value.
failing_case: The stored value is truncated JSON from an interrupted write. The user sees "No recipes yet" with no explanation, adds one recipe, and the original string is overwritten. It can no longer be recovered or inspected.
remediation: Have loadRecipes return a result with an error flag. Show a message in app.js and keep the raw value under a backup key before the first overwrite.
